messages:
Liz Wang: FYI I pulled seastar-6.1b into the onboarding bucket. The repo has a weird license combo — weights are labelled CC-BY-NC-4.0 and there's a separate "third-party-data-terms.pdf" referenced for the training corpus. Can we host this on Redwood Hosted API? Also question: our infra team wants to run int8/4-bit quantization and possibly distribute quantized variants to Dedicated customers. Is that allowed under the license?
Harish Patel: Link? I'll skim the license.
Liz Wang: https://hugrepo.example/seastar-6.1b (private mirror). Key excerpt pasted below.
Liz Wang: ```
Weights: CC-BY-NC-4.0
Training data: "third-party-proprietary-clauses.pdf" (see §3.2)
Redistribution: "Allowed only for non-commercial research and evaluation; commercial hosting prohibited unless explicit permission obtained."
Attribution: must include model card and copyright notice for upstream authors.
```
legal-bot: NOTE: automated scan flagged "non-commercial" restriction on weights. Recommend human legal review before hosting commercially.
Mei Chen: We ran a quick ISO eval on our standard chat/eval harness. Baseline (redwood-std-7b) -> seastar fp16: +1.2 BLEU on conv benchmarks. int8 quant regressed ~2-3% on safety-sensitive prompts (hallucination test).
Jason R: For product: if license forbids commercial hosting, Hosted API is out unless we get permission. Dedicated? Customers who get Dedicated are effectively redistributed copies of runtime + weights — that could be a redistribution problem. Private on-prem might be okay because customer manages everything. Need legal to confirm.
Olivia M: @Liz, thanks for flagging. Two quick things we need: full LICENSE file and the referenced "third-party-proprietary-clauses.pdf". Also we need to know the upstream author/contact for permission requests. Don't assume quantized weights are exempt — derivatives typically count.
Harish Patel: Is there any precedent? We shipped quantized variants of other CC-BY-NC models only to enterprise customers after an addendum. That addendum said: "explicit license to distribute quantized weights for paid hosting and redistribution."
Mei Chen: From a risk POV, quantization changes outputs but not the underlying IP. Our evals show subtle changes that could trigger "derivative" definitions.
Liz Wang: Proposed plan: 1) Pause Hosted ingestion for seastar; 2) Run full license harvest and contact upstream for express permission to host/redistribute quantized variants; 3) Continue evals in Private/Dedicated sandboxes but do not allow customer-side redistribution until legal clears. Sound ok?
Olivia M: Yes. Also ask upstream whether attribution + model card is sufficient or if they require a no-commercial clause to be carried into our TOS. Ask for sample addendum text if possible. I can draft a template once they respond.
Jason R: Quick product Q — if we get permission to host commercialy for Hosted API, do we want to allow Served quantized model variants or only serve quantization at runtime (i.e., runtime quantize but not redistribute weights)? Runtime-only quantization avoids giving out a file but still serves commercial customers.
Mei Chen: Runtime quantization is doable on our serving runtime for many models; accuracy tradeoffs are similar to shipping a quantized checkpoint. But it reduces redistribution risk because we aren't handing out files.
Harish Patel: For Dedicated, customers sometimes ask for the actual checkpoint for on-prem installs. That will be harder.
Liz Wang: Action items: - Liz: attach full license + third-party PDF in this thread (will do) - Olivia: once we have docs, do legal review and draft addendum - Harish/Mei: continue evals in private cluster, flag any major regressions - Jason: block Hosted release until legal clears.
legal-bot: Action logged: legal-review-needed (ticket #LIC-2026-73).
Olivia M: One more ask: please include a short reproduction script for the quantization path you plan to distribute (command + flags). I want to assess whether the quant path is deterministically derivable from original weights or a separate created artifact.
Mei Chen: Will post the quant script. sample: ```bash
python quantize.py --model seastar-6.1b --bits 8 --scheme awq --out seastar-6.1b-awq8.pt
```
Liz Wang: Posted LICENSE and third-party PDF to the shared drive (link in thread). I'll ping upstream contact next.
Olivia M: Thanks — will start review. If upstream grants commercial redistribution for quantized derivatives we can consider a scoped Hosted pilot with attribution requirements + addendum. If not, we restrict to Private/Dedicated (with addendum) and runtime-only hosting for Hosted.
Jason R: OK, keeping product and sales blocked for Hosted until we have an explicit allow.
Liz Wang: Thanks everyone. I'll update once upstream replies. :thumbsup:
